headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: Claude Code can read/write local repo state while cognee ingests sensitive support data via API, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream reuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read and write repo files and use MCP; cognee handles documents and workflows. If cognee outputs are placed in shared files or MCP-fed into Claude Code, prompt-like content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are written into a shared repo file or MCP source that Claude Code reads
IF Claude Code is asked to follow instructions embedded in cognee-generated text
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of cognee outputs into Claude Code prompts
Add a provenance prefix to cognee-generated text
Store cognee outputs in a separate directory not scanned by Claude Code
Review any MCP server mappings before enabling them
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while cognee processes customer support data, personal data, and finance data. If those data are placed in the shared workspace, Claude Code can read them and also has broad network egress. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default terminal workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF customer support or finance data is stored in the same workspace Claude Code can read
IF Claude Code is allowed to transmit those files over broad network egress
mitigations: Move sensitive cognee exports out of Claude Code's workspace
Restrict Claude Code network egress to approved endpoints
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
Redact personal and finance data before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; cognee has session memory and allowlisted network egress. If both operate on the same repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent edits can conflict. Cognee does not advertise filesystem write, so the conflict is narrower than high, but the shared-state pathway exists via files and git.
conditions: IF cognee writes derived outputs into the same repository Claude Code edits
IF both agents mutate the same git branch or shared document without locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep cognee outputs read-only for Claude Code
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and git state, and cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If Claude Code consumes cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or operational changes. Cognee is not documented as a verifier, so the pair needs an explicit validation step.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses cognee-generated decisions or workflows without independent verification
IF those outputs are then committed or executed by Claude Code
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Compare cognee outputs against source data
Mark cognee output as advisory only
Limit Claude Code to dry-run mode for derived actions
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, and environment secrets, while cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data. If those classes are co-mingled, differing retention or residency controls can be violated. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is stored in the same environment as Claude Code secrets or git history
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Separate sensitive datasets from code repositories
Document retention rules for each agent
Avoid storing personal data in git history
Review residency and DPA requirements before syncing data
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and deletion workflows
